basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 9.' and it opens '| Vers. 9. Ecce in tabernaculo est. Abraham foris cum angelis erat; Sara in tabernaculis'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: | Vers. 9. Ecce in tabernaculo est. Abraham foris cum angelis erat; Sara in tabernaculis latebat: quia sapientium et doctorum est aperte praedicare, exemplis alios instituere. Infirmi vero quinque et minus docti se apud se continere debent et doctoribus subdi.
